While the lack of pinned commit in the source (using `branch=main`) means the build is not fully reproducible, this is a common and accepted practice for -git packages in the AUR, allowing users to track the latest development version. This represents a trade-off between reproducibility and freshness, not a security threat.
</details>

<details>
This is the `.SRCINFO` metadata file for `stuff-git`, a `-git` VCS package for the upstream "stuff" file manager hosted at `https://github.com/hyperpuncher/stuff`. The file contains only declarative packaging metadata: pkgdesc, pkgver/pkgrel, url, architecture, license, makedepends, depends, optdepends, provides/conflicts, options, and the source array.

The single source entry is `stuff::git+https://github.com/hyperpuncher/stuff.git#branch=main`, which points at the project's own declared upstream repository over HTTPS — expected and ordinary for a `-git` package. There are no additional sources pointing at unrelated hosts, no binary blobs, no patches, and no scripts referenced. `sha256sums = SKIP` is the required/normal value for a VCS source and is not a concern. The `license = MIT AND Zlib AND ISC` field and dependency list (dbus, fontconfig, libarchive, sdl3, udisks2, wayland, etc.) are all consistent with a lightweight file manager built with Odin.

There is no network exfiltration, no obfuscation or encoding, no `curl`/`wget`/`eval`/`base64` usage, and no file or system modification here — `.SRCINFO` is purely descriptive and is not executed. Minor hygiene observations, none malicious: `pkgver = r0` indicates the version was never regenerated from `git describe`, and `makedepends = odin>=dev_2026_10` requires an unreleased/future Odin snapshot, which may make the package unbuildable for some users.
</details>
